activitySchema.heading: A word we can check
activitySchema.instruction: Sort each word. Can you point to a mark, colour or shape it names? Then explain one choice.

items.label: Thick
items.feedback: Point to a thick line. The word names a mark.

items.label: Rushed
items.feedback: This may describe the process. Add the mark you can see, such as an uneven edge.

items.label: Grey
items.feedback: Point to the grey area. The word names a colour.

items.label: Rubbish
items.feedback: This judgement gives no part to work on. Name a mark that you want to change.

items.label: Curved
items.feedback: Point to a curved edge. The word names a shape.

items.label: Smudged
items.feedback: Point to the smudge. A smudge may be planned or unplanned; ask the maker.

activitySchema.transfer: Choose one word for your sample. Point to its place before you share it.

activitySchema.heading: Label the checks you can see
activitySchema.instruction: Look at A, B and C. Label each sample with a check it shows. Point to the part that lets you check it.

categories.label: I can make three tones that differ
I can draw four gaps of the same width
I can keep my marks inside the edge

items.label: Label A
items.feedback: The three patches go from light to dark. The tones can be checked side by side.

items.label: Label B
items.feedback: Five lines make four gaps. Compare the gaps to check their width.

items.label: Label C
items.feedback: The filled part stays inside the outline. This check uses a clear feature, not a score.

diagram.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 600 190" role="img"><title>Three visible skill checks</title><rect x="1" y="1" width="598" height="188" rx="8" fill="#fffdf7" stroke="#233b4d"/><text x="86" y="32" text-anchor="middle" font-size="21" fill="#233b4d">A</text><text x="276" y="32" text-anchor="middle" font-size="21" fill="#233b4d">B</text><text x="500" y="32" text-anchor="middle" font-size="21" fill="#233b4d">C</text><rect x="25" y="55" width="36" height="70" fill="#e2e8ed" stroke="#233b4d"/><rect x="68" y="55" width="36" height="70" fill="#8998a5" stroke="#233b4d"/><rect x="111" y="55" width="36" height="70" fill="#233b4d" stroke="#233b4d"/><line x1="220" y1="55" x2="220" y2="125" stroke="#233b4d" stroke-width="3"/><line x1="248" y1="55" x2="248" y2="125" stroke="#233b4d" stroke-width="3"/><line x1="276" y1="55" x2="276" y2="125" stroke="#233b4d" stroke-width="3"/><line x1="304" y1="55" x2="304" y2="125" stroke="#233b4d" stroke-width="3"/><line x1="332" y1="55" x2="332" y2="125" stroke="#233b4d" stroke-width="3"/><rect x="440" y="48" width="120" height="85" fill="none" stroke="#233b4d" stroke-width="3"/><rect x="448" y="56" width="104" height="69" fill="#af5940"/></svg>
diagram.alt: A shows three patches from light to dark. B shows five evenly spaced lines. C shows colour inside an outline.
diagram.caption: Three visible skill checks. Original teaching drawing.

activitySchema.discussion: Which check could help with your skill? You may choose a count or a feature. Say how someone could check it.
activitySchema.staffNote: These are examples, not compulsory goals. Accept any clear, checkable measure suited to the learner’s art form. The annotation is practice; their own skill card records their own choice.

activitySchema.heading: Predict, then check a practice trial
activitySchema.instruction: These are made-up model trials. First predict. Check the model with your adult when you are ready. Your own result may differ.

items.label: The same soft pencil presses harder. What might change?

options.label: The marks may get darker
The paper must get bigger

items.feedback: Model result: the marks got darker; the paper size stayed the same. Test what happens with your own pencil.

items.label: A fine pencil is swapped for thick chalk. What else might change?

options.label: Nothing but the colour
The marks may get wider

items.feedback: Model result: the chalk marks were wider. A new tool can change more than one feature.

items.label: The tool, paper, time and box size stay the same. What do you predict we can compare?

options.label: The first and last marks fairly
How every artist will improve

items.feedback: Model check: these two boxes can be compared. They may show change or no clear change. Neither result proves what every artist will do.

activitySchema.discussion: Say which prediction the model supported. Keep the same tool and box size in your own practice. Record what really happens.
activitySchema.staffNote: Ask for predictions before opening explanations. The reported results belong to the labelled fictional trials. They are not guaranteed effects or evidence of pupil progress. Accept a reasoned different prediction, then discuss the supplied result.

activitySchema.heading: Ask for a useful next step
activitySchema.instruction: The maker wants more even gaps in box four. Choose the question that will help, then say why.

options.label: Is my strip good?
Which gap in box four should I change, and how?
Tell me everything about my art.

items.label: Which question should the maker ask?
items.feedback: This names the part and asks for an action. The other questions may start a talk but need more focus to give a clear next step.

activitySchema.transfer: Point to one part of the model. Make your own question, then hear a partner’s suggestion.

activitySchema.heading: Keep the before, then try the change
activitySchema.instruction: Rebuild this model order: read the feedback, keep the before, try the change, then compare. Choose 1 to 4 for each card.

items.label: Try the chosen change, then stop
items.feedback: Stop after the planned trial so you can look at what it did.

items.label: Read the feedback and name one action
items.feedback: First decide which part and action you will try.

items.label: Compare before and after; record what changed
items.feedback: Use the two states to explain what happened. No improvement yet is a real result.

items.label: Keep a photo, copy or unchanged sample
items.feedback: Keep the starting marks before you alter them. A ring only shows a place.

activitySchema.transfer: Tell a partner how you will keep your before state. They check that it survives the change.
activitySchema.staffNote: This is the demonstrated model order. Keeping the before copy before reading the feedback is also safe: both must happen before changing the work. Accept and discuss that justified order.

activitySchema.heading: Spot the gap in a review
activitySchema.instruction: Each made-up summary has a gap. Spot the error, then say one way to fix it. A plain, honest result is enough.

items.label: “It got better.” What is missing?

options.label: A long word
The goal and a detail we can check

items.feedback: Name the goal and the part that changed. Better alone does not say what happened.

items.label: “My proof is somewhere in my files.” What needs fixing?

options.label: The place to find the work
The choice to keep the work

items.feedback: Give the actual file and page, slide or timecode. Check that someone can open it.

items.label: “I changed nothing, so I must say I improved.” What is wrong?

options.label: It hides the real result
It uses the word I

items.feedback: No clear change yet is an honest result. Say what you tried and what you learnt from it.

activitySchema.discussion: Improve one of the model notes. Then check your own goal, result, learning and evidence link.
activitySchema.staffNote: Use the current model key. Do not require improvement where the work does not show it. The learner reviews their own practice; correcting this model is not their Part A evidence.

activitySchema.heading: Label a choice, then add your view
activitySchema.instruction: Label the craft choice in each panel. Then annotate one panel: say what you notice and what it does for you. You do not have to like it.

categories.label: Scale: the size of a shape

items.label: Label panel A
items.feedback: Two colours meet at an edge. You can name the choice, then give your own response.

items.label: Label panel B
items.feedback: The circles have the same colour but different sizes. Scale is the size choice.

diagram.alt: Panel A shows two coloured blocks. Panel B shows one small and one large circle in the same colour.
diagram.caption: Two craft choices to notice. Original teaching drawing.

activitySchema.discussion: Point to one detail. Tell a partner its effect on you. They may see it differently. Add a short label or spoken note with your reason.
activitySchema.staffNote: The labels describe observable choices. Effects and preferences are personal; do not mark a different supported response wrong. This drawing rehearses noticing, not participation in a real audience experience.

activitySchema.heading: Build a useful review row
activitySchema.instruction: Match each practice note to a column. If it needs a detail or reason first, choose Needs more detail. Then improve one note together.

items.label: The room goes dark for ten seconds.
items.feedback: This tells us which moment the writer noticed.

items.label: It was a really good hour.
items.feedback: This view can start a review. Add a moment and a reason so a reader knows what worked.

items.label: The maker left the joins showing.
items.feedback: This names a choice the maker made in the work.

items.label: My eye goes to the red first.
items.feedback: This describes an effect on this viewer. Other viewers may respond differently.

items.label: The practice label says this work was made for young children.
items.feedback: The label supports the audience claim. A low label alone would not.

items.label: I liked all of it.
items.feedback: Your feeling matters. Choose one detail and say why it led to that view.

activitySchema.discussion: Choose one Needs more detail note. Add a detail from the practice work; keep your own view. These are practice notes, not a record of an event.

activitySchema.heading: Build the practice review
activitySchema.instruction: Use the drawing. Put these notes in the model order: name a choice, judge how it works, then explain its effect. Choose a different position for each note.

items.label: My eye follows the gap down the page.
items.feedback: The last note gives the effect on this viewer.

items.label: The lines are close together.
items.feedback: Start with the choice you can point to in the drawing.

items.label: The gap stays clear from top to bottom.
items.feedback: Then judge how the choice works, using a detail we can check.

The lines bend slightly. diagram.caption: Original practice drawing. It is not attributed to a real artist.
diagram.alt: Six dark lines bend slightly down the page around a clear central gap.

activitySchema.discussion: Read the three notes as one review. Point to what supports the view. You may respond differently: give your own reason. This is practice, not evidence of an arts experience.
activitySchema.staffNote: Accept other spoken review orders once pupils can distinguish the three jobs. This order is a scaffold, not an award rule. Do not grade a pupil’s personal response to the drawing.

activitySchema.heading: Spot a claim we cannot use yet
activitySchema.instruction: These are made-up source notes, not facts about a named artist. Spot the error in each note. Say what you would check or change.

items.label: The source says bronze. My note says wood. What needs fixing?

options.label: The material in my note
The fact that I kept a source

items.feedback: Check the full source and correct the material. Keep the source beside the corrected note.

items.label: “I like its curved edge, so everyone must like it.” What is wrong?

options.label: A curve cannot be noticed
My view is treated as everyone’s view

items.feedback: Keep your own view and reason. Other people may respond differently.

items.label: “The artist felt sad.” There is no source for that claim. What should I do?

options.label: State it as a fact
Check a source or leave the claim open

items.feedback: Do not guess an artist’s thoughts. You can describe the work and your own response without that claim.

activitySchema.discussion: Choose your own real practitioner from the checked pack. Keep a named work, a source and your own reason for choosing them.
activitySchema.staffNote: All three statements are explicit model errors, not sourced biography. Keep personal views distinct from checked facts. Retain the real-practitioner requirement and the learner’s own choice.

activitySchema.heading: Four questions about one artist
activitySchema.instruction: Sort the checked Hepworth model notes by the question each answers best. Then explain one link to another heading.

items.label: Hepworth was born in Wakefield.
items.feedback: This is a public life fact. Check the 1903 section of the Estate biography.

items.label: She studied sculpture at the Royal College of Art.
items.feedback: This is a step in her training. Check the 1921–24 section. Training can also shape practice.

items.label: She learnt marble carving from Giovanni Ardini.
items.feedback: This tells us about a making skill. Check the 1925 section. It also links to her training.

items.label: Assembly of Sea Forms is a white marble sculpture.
items.feedback: This names a real work and its material. Check the sculpture’s own caption.

activitySchema.discussion: Choose one note. Tell a partner which source would let them check it. A note can link to two headings; explain that link instead of counting one thin fact four times.
activitySchema.staffNote: The key shows the best fit for these model questions. Accept a reasoned second connection, especially training and practice. Do not mark a supported connection as wrong just because it crosses a heading.

activitySchema.heading: Make the plan teachable
activitySchema.instruction: Choose the note in each pair that helps a new learner take part. Then change one note so it fits the art skill you want to share.

items.label: Which note gives a clear step to show?
items.feedback: Showing the pencil angle gives the learner something they can see and try.

options.label: Be good at drawing.
Show the angle of the pencil.

items.label: Which note gives the learner a turn?
items.feedback: A try on scrap lets the learner use the skill while you watch and help.

options.label: Try a mark on your own scrap.
Watch me do it all.

items.label: Which note checks the skill?
items.feedback: Meeting edges gives a clear check for this fold. Asking about enjoyment can be useful as an extra question.

options.label: Only ask if it was nice.
Check if the two edges meet.

activitySchema.discussion: Pick one pair and explain your choice to a partner or staff member. Add the learner action or check to your own plan. Your skill may use a different tool or action.

activitySchema.heading: Predict a learner response
activitySchema.instruction: Read each made-up rehearsal. Make your prediction first, then check the model with your adult. Real learners may respond in other ways.

items.label: A hand blocks the view. We move the sample. What might that help?

options.label: The learner can see the next step
The learner must finish at once

items.feedback: Model result: the learner saw the grip and asked to see it again. We checked their view before continuing.

items.label: Three steps were said at once. We show just the first. What may change?

options.label: All questions will stop forever
The next try may be easier to start

items.feedback: Model result: the learner tried the first step, then asked for help with the next. We gave one clear cue at a time.

items.label: The learner asks to pause. We agree. What does that allow?

options.label: A real choice about taking part
A claim that the whole share is done

items.feedback: Model result: the learner watched for a while. We recorded the pause honestly and agreed what could happen next.

activitySchema.discussion: Compare a prediction with the model result. During your own share, ask and listen. Record the response you get, not the one you hoped for.
activitySchema.staffNote: Predictions are tentative, not judgments about the learner. These are fictional rehearsals. Actual delivery, a willing learner, feedback and an honest status remain required; a practice answer cannot stand in for delivery.

activitySchema.heading: Label where the work belongs
activitySchema.instruction: Label A, B, C and D on the map. Then add one real file name and its page, slide or time. Write Gap if the work is not there.

categories.label: My art skill and how it changed
An arts event and the view I shared
The real artist I found out about
My skills share: plan, do and review

items.label: Label Part A
items.feedback: A shows you taking part in art, trying a skill and saying what changed.

items.label: Label Part B
items.feedback: B shows the real arts event and your view shared with someone. This model is not that event.

items.label: Label Part C
items.feedback: C names a real artist. Keep what you found, why you chose them and your source.

items.label: Label Part D
items.feedback: D shows your plan, the real share, what your learner said or did, and your review.

diagram.alt: Four boxes: Part A at upper left, Part B at upper right, Part C at lower left and Part D at lower right.
diagram.caption: A map of the four parts. Original teaching drawing.

activitySchema.discussion: Add one real place to find the work. Ask a willing checker to find it. Keep all four parts in no more than ten files. A file can hold more than one page.
activitySchema.staffNote: The four boxes organise the four parts; they do not require four separate files. The cap remains ten evidence files overall. Do not mark missing evidence as present or count this practice map as completed arts work.
